title: Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now
key_facts: Microsoft says post-quantum planning often focuses on protecting encrypted data but authentication systems (certificates, trust anchors, PKI services, devices) must also change.
Microsoft launched its Post-Quantum Cryptography TLS Pilot Program on 27 Aug 2026 for approved certificate authorities in its Trusted Root Program.
The pilot tests certificates using the ML-DSA-87 signature algorithm; its certificates are not publicly trusted and must not be used in production or public websites.
Seven pilot roots were added in August 2026, operated by ComSign, DigiCert, HARICA, IdenTrust Services, Sectigo, Shanghai Electronic Certification Authority and SSL.com.
Admissions are rolling through the end of 2026; ML-DSA certificates can be tested on supported Windows 11 systems from the 28 July 2026 updates.
Microsoft advises organisations to inventory certificate-dependent systems, assess vendor roadmaps, find long-lived infrastructure and build non-production test environments.
quote_evidence: Certificates issued through the pilot are not publicly trusted and are intended solely for interoperability and ecosystem-readiness testing in closed environments, custom applications, and enterprise testbeds.
Organizations should view post-quantum readiness as a multi-year planning effort rather than a future migration project.
why_it_matters_hint: Microsoft is telling IT teams to start testing quantum-resistant certificates now.
notes: Vendor guidance post, not a mandate. The blog expands the abbreviation as "Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signal Algorithm" (apparent slip for Signature). The pilot itself dates from 27 Aug 2026.
